content.value_statement: Timeouts and conflicting receipts can leave delivery status unclear and make retries risky. This skill guides evidence matching and produces a bounded reconciliation record without resending.
actual_capabilities: Guides matching receipts to the original request ID, target, submission time, and submitted content fingerprint.
Separates accepted, sent, delivered, read, definitely not sent, and outcome unknown using documented channel meanings.
Distinguishes relevant receipts from newer records for different targets, requests, or replacement attachments.
Structures a reconciliation record with acceptance requirements, observations, identity matches, evidence gaps, and a conclusion.
Defines one original-request lookup with an attempt cap or expiry and an explicit stopping result.
Keeps proposed checks separate from completed checks and limits simulations to supplied evidence.
limitations: Provides instructions, not a delivery service or bundled status-query integration.
Cannot confirm delivery without trustworthy evidence linked to the original request.
Cannot resolve undocumented status meanings or unproven identifier aliases.
Does not send, resend, or guarantee remote idempotency.

use_cases.title: Resolve a customer upload timeout
use_cases.description: Compare the original upload with available receipts and explain whether delivery is established without asking the customer to upload again.

use_cases.title: Review conflicting dispatch records
use_cases.description: Separate records for different recipients or identifiers before deciding whether the original outbound request meets its acceptance requirement.

use_cases.title: Check a replacement attachment
use_cases.description: Compare submitted fingerprints when a same-named replacement file appears, preserving unknown status when the original delivery lacks matching evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Review one timed-out submission
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile this timed-out submission using the supplied receipt: [request and receipt]. State whether the required acceptance level is met. Do not resend.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: one original request and one available receipt.

prompt_templates.title: Compare conflicting receipts
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these receipts for the original request: [ID, target, submission time, fingerprint, and observations]. Match identity before comparing timestamps. Explain excluded records and report the supported status.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: multiple receipts may describe different requests.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile a replacement attachment
prompt_templates.prompt: The upload timed out and a same-named file now has a different fingerprint: [evidence]. Distinguish the original payload from the replacement. Provide a record and at most one proposed lookup.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: filenames match but submitted content differs.

prompt_templates.title: Define a bounded unresolved-case handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Use only this simulated evidence: [original identity, possible aliases, receipts, channel definitions, and access limits]. Preserve unresolved identity mappings and mark missing fields. Define one original-only lookup with a one-attempt cap and explicit stop result. Do not contact a real channel or resend.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: ambiguous identifiers and unavailable status access require a bounded handoff.

best_practices: Provide the original request ID, target, submission time, and submitted content fingerprint.
Include receipt sources, observation times, raw labels, and documented channel meanings.
Set one lookup limit and stop when acceptance is met or the limit is reached.
anti_patterns: Do not resend with the same ID, a new ID, or a test click to resolve uncertainty.
Do not treat matching filenames, newer timestamps, or unrelated receipts as proof of original-request delivery.
Do not turn timeouts, zero local counters, or empty searches into definitive failure or unlimited polling.

faq.question: Does this skill send or resend requests?
faq.answer: No. It reconciles an existing attempt and explicitly prohibits replaying the original business action.

faq.question: Does a timeout prove that delivery failed?
faq.answer: No. A timeout can occur after remote acceptance, so the original result remains unknown without stronger evidence.

faq.question: Are sent and delivered interchangeable?
faq.answer: No. Use the channel's documented meanings and compare the supported receipt level with the user's acceptance requirement.

faq.question: What if request fields or status access are missing?
faq.answer: Mark missing fields as not provided and deliver the current record. Describe any lookup as proposed, not completed.

faq.question: Does the skill include delivery service integrations?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow and report template. Actual status access depends on tools and permissions available in the surrounding environment.

faq.question: When should reconciliation stop?
faq.answer: Close when matching evidence meets the required level. Otherwise stop at the lookup cap or expiry and preserve unresolved status.
